subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction retry creates orphan fork in parentId chain (dead-end branch breaks chain reconstruction)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a load-time repair that deletes only dead-end same-parent compaction retry entries from persisted session JSONL, or require write-side retry prevention before repairing existing files?
rationale: The remaining decision changes persisted session state by dropping structurally valid entries that are judged semantically superseded, so automation should not decide the repair policy alone.

options.title: Approve narrow repair and refresh PR
options.body: Refresh or replace the linked PR over current main, integrate the incremental repair cache path, and land the compaction-only dead-end deletion rule with regression and upgrade coverage.

options.title: Require write-side prevention first
options.body: Pause the repair PR until compaction retry writes become idempotent or otherwise unable to create same-parent compaction siblings.

options.title: Split repair and prevention
options.body: Land a narrowly approved existing-file repair now and track source-side duplicate prevention as follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow repair and refresh PR
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the linked PR over current main, integrate the incremental repair cache path, and land the compaction-only dead-end deletion rule with regression and upgrade coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent validated transcript cache work is the current repair boundary the linked PR must fit before the policy can land safely.
